evidence.requirements: Every brief item is met. Start page: title, date/time, EUR price and "<n> seats left" (views.js:47-66, start.jpg). Book links read exactly "Book <title>" (views.js:58). Form has labels Name, Email and Guests, a min=1/max=8 guests field and a "Book" button (views.js:79-91). Seat limit and invalid input are checked on the server and shown in a role=alert block above the form (validation.js:29-38, server.js:173-177). Confirmation shows the heading "Booking confirmed", tasting, guests, total and reference (views.js:96-115, confirmation.jpg: 2 x EUR 32 = EUR 64). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button, with the password read from STAFF_PASSWORD (index.js:4, views.js:133-147). Bookings are grouped by tasting with name, email, guests, reference and a Cancel button (views.js:150-190, staff.jpg). Cancelling frees the seats (store.js:68-70). PORT defaults to 3000 (index.js:3). Bookings are in memory, the app starts empty and the interface is in English. One caveat: in form.jpg the browser's native type=email check blocked the submit, so the page's own error message is not visible. The server-side message exists and is tested (app.test.js:125-146).
evidence.correctness: Seats left are computed from the live bookings (store.js:23-31). Validation runs after the body has been read, and the check and insert then run in one synchronous step (server.js:162-185), so concurrent requests cannot oversell. store.book re-checks the seat count as a guard (store.js:46-50). Guests must match /^\d+$/ and fall in 1..8, which rejects 2.5, 'two', empty, 0 and 9 (validation.js:29-32). Full-house and exact-fit cases are handled (validation.js:33-37, tested at app.test.js:156-173). Cancelling deletes the booking and its confirmation then returns 404 (app.test.js:267-284). References are unique and avoid look-alike characters (store.js:33-42). Small flaws: the staff summary reads "1 guests booked" (views.js:175, staff.jpg). A fully booked tasting still shows an active Book button on the start page (views.js:58).
evidence.security: All output goes through esc(), which covers & < > " ' (views.js:4-12), and XSS is tested (app.test.js:175-186). The password is compared as SHA-256 digests with timingSafeEqual (server.js:40-46). Sessions use a 32-byte random token in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie with an 8-hour server-side expiry, and sign-out deletes the session (server.js:48-67, 136-149). Cancelling requires a session and POST (server.js:151-157). SameSite=Strict plus form-action 'self' in the CSP limits CSRF. Form bodies are capped at 16 KB (server.js:215-228). The app sends CSP, nosniff and X-Frame-Options DENY headers. If STAFF_PASSWORD is empty, sign-in is disabled (server.js:130-132). There are no secrets in the code. Two gaps remain: the cookie has no Secure flag and sign-in has no rate limiting. The README lists both as pre-launch steps (README.md:55-58).
evidence.code_quality: The code is split into clear modules: tastings data, store, validation, views and the server with routing, plus a thin entry point. Functions are small and well named, and comments are sparse and useful (store.js:8-10, server.js:38-39). The store can be injected and the clock passed in, which makes the code testable without extra abstraction layers. Error handling uses a status-carrying error for 413 and falls back to a 500 page (server.js:188-198). Minor: in the 413 path sendHtml does not check res.headersSent, unlike the 500 path.
evidence.tests: app.test.js has about 25 tests against a live server. They cover the listing contents, exact Book link text, form labels and limits, booking with confirmation and total, a table of invalid inputs, value re-fill, seat-limit and full-house boundaries, and escaping. Staff tests cover the login form, wrong password, disabled sign-in, grouping by tasting, cancel freeing seats, cancel without a session, a forged cookie, sign-out, cookie flags and session expiry with an injected clock. Body limits, 404, 405 and headers are also tested. The tests check behaviour, not internals. There is no explicit concurrent-request test, but the synchronous design makes one unnecessary.
evidence.ux_design: The screenshots show a clean, consistent wine-red and cream theme that suits a winery. start.jpg has clear cards with a definition-list layout and prominent book buttons. The form page repeats date, price and seats left (form.jpg). The staff page has tidy per-tasting cards with booked/left summaries and a Sign out button (staff.jpg). Weaknesses: dates are raw ISO "2026-11-06 18:00" rather than a guest-friendly format. The confirmation page is plain text without a card and the reference is not visually emphasised (confirmation.jpg). Cancel happens with no confirmation step. In form.jpg the invalid email is only outlined and no visible error text appears in the page. Full tastings keep an active Book button. The staff summary shows "1 guests booked".
evidence.accessibility: The page sets lang=en, has a main landmark and a proper heading hierarchy. Every input has a <label for> (views.js:80-89, 141). Errors use role=alert so screen readers announce them (views.js:40). The empty action column has a visually-hidden "Actions" header (views.js:157). Inputs have a visible focus outline (style.css:150-153). Contrast is good: muted #6e6360 on #faf6ef is about 5.4:1, and white on #6b1e2e and #a4262c is high. Gaps: no aria-invalid or aria-describedby ties an error to its field. Focus is not moved to the error summary. The repeated "Cancel" buttons have no accessible name that says which booking they cancel (views.js:167).
evidence.simplicity: There are no runtime or dev dependencies: node:http, node:crypto and node:test only (package.json). About 600 lines of source plus CSS, which fits the problem. There is no framework and no needless layers. The store is a plain closure over Maps.

strengths: Correct, server-enforced seat logic that cannot oversell: validation and insert run in one synchronous step, a guard sits in the store, and the boundary cases are tested.
Strong security for the scope: consistent escaping, timing-safe password check, random server-side sessions with HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict and expiry, CSP and security headers, and a body size limit.
Zero dependencies, clean module split and a meaningful test suite that maps closely onto every requirement in the brief.
issues: Staff sign-in has no rate limiting and the session cookie has no Secure flag. Both are documented in README.md:55-58 but not implemented, so a deployment step is needed before going public.

UX rough edges: Cancel removes a guest's booking with no confirmation, dates are raw ISO strings, fully booked tastings still show an active Book button, and the staff page says "1 guests booked" (views.js:175).
Accessibility gaps around errors and actions: no aria-invalid or aria-describedby linking messages to fields, and identical "Cancel" button names give no context about which booking they cancel.
review.verdict: A compact, dependency-free and well-tested app that meets every requirement in the brief, with correct seat handling and better-than-expected security. The remaining work is polish (date formatting, a cancel confirmation, plural wording, ARIA error wiring) plus HTTPS/Secure cookie and login rate limiting at deployment, so it is close to shippable as is.
